subject: Equinox reserved capacity ask — hedge triggers, fallback SKUs, and approval path
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@equinox.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@equinox.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Reserve request & price-protection ask for enterprise pilot

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited. We are preparing a contract for a 12-month reserved capacity commitment to support our inferencing pipeline (peak 1.2k tokens/s sustained, spikes to 3k). Before we move to procurement, two items are blocking us:

1) GPU price volatility: our CFO wants a short clause or mechanism that prevents a >20% increase in per-token cost year-over-year without a review/credit.
2) Fallback SKUs: we need a clear list of certified fallback model/sku options (lower-cost quantized variants) in case specific GPUs are constrained.

Could you share a proposed structure (trigger, cap, and who signs off) and a contact for legal to review redlines? Procurement would like a single SOW and a DocuSign-ready packet.

Appreciate a prompt turnaround — procurement is aiming to finalize by next Friday.

Thanks,
Samir
VP, Cloud Engineering
Equinox AI
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@equinox.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserve request & price-protection ask for enterprise pilot

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear ask. High level proposal below; I'll loop in Finance & Ops for the exact thresholds and approval flow.

Proposal (high level):
- Term: 12-month reserved pool, with monthly utilization reporting and quarterly checkpoints.
- Price protection trigger: if underlying GPU index (we use publicly available SKU spot/contract index + our procurement avg) increases >18% vs baseline, we provide a one-time credit equal to the differential up to a cap, OR allow a single-term reprice discussion with mutually-agreed arbitration.
- Fallback SKUs: we will certify 2 quantized variants per model family as official fallbacks (NQ8 and INT4-equivalent). We will list fallback SKUs in the SOW appendix.
- Approval path: discounts / credits up to 12% can be approved by Sales Ops; anything beyond requires Finance + Legal sign-off (I'll introduce Marcus and Kim).

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus to confirm sustainable discount/credit thresholds and any finance constraints.
2) Aditya to confirm ops feasibility (SKU list, burst/overflow behavior).
3) I'll prepare a short redlineable SOW + appendix and share a DocuSign link once legal confirms language.

I'm attaching a rough SKU mix we discussed for context.

Best,
Tessa
Senior Account Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SKU_mix.xlsx (spreadsheet — SKU allocation by month)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserve request & price-protection ask for enterprise pilot

Tessa / team — quick finance view.

We've seen requests like this from two mid-market deals recently. Practical guardrails to keep:
- Credit versus reprice: prefer a credit mechanism (one-time adjustment) rather than open reprice conversations. Credits preserve revenue visibility.
- Thresholds: 18% trigger with an annual cap equal to 6% of ARR for the deal seems reasonable (keeps exposure bounded).
- Discount authority: Sales Ops ok for up to 12% off list. Anything >12% requires FP&A and CRO approval.
- Escalation cadence: If index delta >18% and projected monthly impact exceeds 1% of Redwood's fleet spend, escalate to finance execs — we need to protect overall hedges.

If Equinox strongly requests a pass-through cap, we can propose a maximum annual pass-through of 10% of the cost side, beyond which Redwood covers the remainder via our procurement hedge. But that needs legal wording and Ops confirmation re: SKU substitutions.

I'll earmark provisional authority subject to final SOW language / accounting treatment.

—Marcus
Director, Finance (Revenue Ops)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@equinox.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserve request & price-protection ask for enterprise pilot

Hi Samir — ops note on fallbacks and burst behavior.

- Fallback SKUs: We can certify two fallback variants per major model family (quantized NQ8 and highly-quantized INT4). Fallbacks are functionally validated but have slight latency/quality trade-offs; we will document expected percent change in latency and a short QA checklist.
- Burst: The reserved pool can be configured with a 25% monthly burst buffer to handle spikes; overflow beyond that uses our shared spot pool at market rates (we can set a soft cap for Equinox).
- Implementation: we'll list exact model variant names in the SOW appendix and provide a migration plan (runtime routing + automated fallback).

Attachment: pricing_matrix.csv (ops cost assumptions mapped to SKU types). Happy to run a short technical call next week to walk through the fallback perf tradeoffs with your infra team.

Thanks,
Aditya
Head of Serving Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Samir Gupta <samir@equinox.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@equinox.ai>
Date: 2026-06-22T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserve request & price-protection ask for enterprise pilot

Tessa / Marcus / Aditya — this looks good and much clearer than our starting point. A few clarifications before we send to legal: 

- Can we get the credit mechanism spelled with an explicit example in the SOW (baseline price = X, index jump = Y%, credit = Z)? Procurement needs concrete math.
- Equinox prefers a maximum annual pass-through of 8% (instead of 10%). We're comfortable with credits up to the Finance-prescribed cap you mentioned (6% of ARR) but would like a hard cap on direct pass-through to customers.
- Please include the fallback SKU names and an explicit QA/perf delta table in the appendix.

When will you have a redline-ready SOW? Also please include a single DocuSign packet (SOW + Exhibit A: Pricing & Fallback SKUs).

Samir
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@equinox.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-22T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserve request & price-protection ask for enterprise pilot

Samir — thanks for the quick feedback. Redwood sign-off summary below so procurement can proceed: 

1) Credit mechanism: we will include an explicit worked example in Exhibit A showing baseline price, index movement, and resulting credit calculation.
2) Annual pass-through cap: approved at 8% maximum pass-through to Equinox (we will cover excess above 8% up to the Finance cap via a one-time credit subject to the 6% ARR exposure limit Marcus documented).
3) Fallback SKUs & QA table: Aditya to include explicit variant names and perf deltas in the appendix.
4) Discount authority: Sales Ops can finalize pricing up to 12% discount; anything above that will require Marcus and me to sign.

I've asked Legal to prepare a redline SOW and will send a DocuSign packet once the SOW is ready. Expect the first draft by EOD tomorrow.

—Kimberly Park
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redlined_SOW.pdf (placeholder — legal will produce final redline)
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/link/eqx-sow-DS-44321
